title: MrBeast's Ramayana Appearance Puts Spotlight on His $200,000 Event Fee
excerpt: The world's most-subscribed YouTuber joined Ranbir Kapoor and the 'Ramayana: Part 1' team at a Mumbai event on September 26 — the same night a new collaboration between MrBeast and producer Namit Malhotra was revealed.
body:
• MrBeast's reported appearance fee starts at $200,000 (about ₹1.67 crore) for live or virtual events, according to Variety India.
  • The world's most-subscribed YouTuber attended a "Ramayana: Part 1" promotional event in Mumbai on September 26, joining Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and the film's team.
  • On stage, Ranbir Kapoor guided MrBeast through a "Jai Shree Ram" chant after the YouTuber was prompted by the press.
  • Producer Namit Malhotra also revealed a new collaboration with MrBeast on "The Angry Birds Movie 3," in which Malhotra is producing and MrBeast will voice a character.

Jimmy Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, does not come cheap. The world's most-subscribed YouTuber is reportedly available for live and virtual event appearances at a starting fee of $200,000 — roughly ₹1.67 crore at current exchange rates — a figure that gives some measure of the commercial value attached to the MrBeast brand.

The fee came under the spotlight after Donaldson appeared at a promotional event for "Ramayana: Part 1" in Mumbai on September 26, joining lead actors Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Ravie Dubey alongside director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra. As of late September, Donaldson's main YouTube channel had around 518 million subscribers and more than 140 billion views, He became the first individual creator to cross 500 million YouTube subscribers in June 2026.

Context & Background

The Mumbai event — held at DNEG Prime Focus — brought together the core team of one of Indian cinema's most ambitious productions. Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Ravie Dubey play Lord Rama, Sita and Lord Lakshman respectively, while the film also stars Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman, with music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations, and distributed globally by Sony Pictures, excluding India.

At the Mumbai event he greeted the press with a brief "Dhanyawaad" (thank you) and stayed through the film's presentation, which included an exclusive behind-the-scenes reel detailing the scale of the film's visual effects work, along with plans for character-led spin-offs, merchandise lines and VR experiences tied to the Ramayana universe.

The evening's most shared moment arrived when members of the media began chanting "Jai Shri Ram, MrBeast." Unsure how to respond, Donaldson turned to Kapoor for help, and the actor guided him through the chant and went viral. Kapoor also took the opportunity to explain the cultural weight of the epic to the American creator, describing Lord Rama as "'Maryada Purushottam', which symbolizes a righteous man" who "sacrificed it all to fulfil his father's promise," and explaining dharma as "one's commitment to duty."

"Lord Rama is the perfect man, and through this film, you can have a brief introduction to our culture, history and where it all began."

— Ranbir Kapoor, actor

Impact & Analysis

Bringing MrBeast into the orbit of "Ramayana" is a deliberate piece of global marketing. The makers have positioned the film as a story that can travel beyond India, and a creator whose videos routinely attract hundreds of millions of viewers gives the production access to an audience far outside the traditional Bollywood ecosystem. Whether his involvement extends beyond the Mumbai appearance remains unclear — Variety India's focus was the event fee — but the crossover value is obvious in both directions: the film gets global visibility, and the YouTuber gets a front-row seat to one of the world's oldest stories.

The appearance also produced a genuine surprise. Malhotra announced on stage that he and MrBeast are collaborating on "The Angry Birds Movie 3," which his team is producing, with MrBeast set to voice a character. The YouTuber appeared caught off-guard by the news, quipping that he had not known about the collaboration until that day — a line that drew laughs and became the night's other big headline.

Diaspora Angle

For the Indian diaspora, the image of the planet's biggest YouTuber chanting "Jai Shree Ram" on a Mumbai stage — and explaining nothing about why he is there — is a small signal of how far Indian popular culture has travelled. "Ramayana: Part 1" is explicitly being made for a worldwide audience, with Hindi and English versions and a global theatrical rollout; diaspora audiences, especially in North America and Europe, are likely to be among the first to see it in IMAX.

What's Next

"Ramayana: Part 1," officially titled "Ramayana: Rise of a Legend," is set for a worldwide theatrical release on November 6, 2026, in IMAX, 3D and premium large formats, with the second part following on Diwali 2027. The Mumbai event, which reportedly ran more than three hours late — drawing grumbles from the waiting media — suggests the film's promotional campaign is only gathering momentum as the release approaches.
